module.name: core
module.spec: Validate must reject duplicate spec IDs, duplicate marker IDs, edges referencing unknown endpoints, self-edges, duplicate edges, or directed cycles among spec-spec edges. Edges whose endpoint does not exist (broken edges — typically a typo in a <ref> target) are NOT rejected here; they surface as EDGE_BROKEN events in derived closures so the user can fix the spec text or restore the missing spec. Validation must pass when all references are consistent. See principles.specs_are_truth.

Given a TodoAction with a Scan covering all spec and marker IDs, the algorithm runs DeriveClosures: NODE_CHANGED for baseline nodes whose scan hash differs; EDGE_ADDED for spec-spec edges in scan but not baseline (link edges are user-curated and never appear in scan); EDGE_REMOVED for spec-spec edges in baseline but not scan; EDGE_BROKEN for scan edges whose To endpoint does not exist; NODE_ADDED/NODE_REMOVED surfaced when reconciled baseline hash is empty. When a node has been deleted from disk, the reconciler keeps it with a sentinel empty-string scan hash and Deleted=true so closure derivation can flag it. The algorithm also runs DeriveOrphans (see core.reachability) to flag specs with no path from any marker. The returned EvaluatedState propagates Specs, Markers, Edges, Closures, and Orphans. See principles.friction.

Given a ResetClosureAction targeting a closure by its 8-character hash, the algorithm re-derives closures from scan+baseline, finds the closure with matching hash, then applies each event: NODE_CHANGED sets baseline hash to scan hash; EDGE_ADDED adds the edge to baseline; EDGE_REMOVED removes the edge from baseline; NODE_REMOVED deletes the node and filters its edges; EDGE_BROKEN is a no-op (the user must fix the scan). Closures containing ONLY broken-edge events are refused with ErrBrokenEdgeNotResettable. The returned EvaluatedState propagates Specs, Markers, Edges, and the full derived Closures. See principles.friction for why reset is per-closure.

The scan must provide a hash for every spec and marker in the context, including empty string for deleted entries. Missing hashes for known specs or markers cause an error. Unknown spec or marker hashes in the scan that are not in the context also cause an error. See principles.specs_are_truth.

DeriveClosures implements provenance propagation: drift on a node walks the citer chain (cited → citer) so reviewers see the upstream impact of any change. For each seed (a node with a drift event), closure membership = seed + transitive citers. Marker seeds additionally include their outgoing-edge targets (the specs they link to) so reviewers can verify the marker still implements the linked spec. Spec seeds do NOT include their cited specs (those specs' text is independent of the seed's drift). Closure membership determines a stable 8-character hash (first 8 hex chars of SHA1(sorted node IDs + sorted undirected edge keys)); closures with identical hashes merge with combined events. Markers cannot be cited, so drift through a marker stops there — this is the only retained asymmetry between specs and markers. Closures are strictly disjoint across seeds: a non-seed citer that cites multiple drifted specs appears in each spec's closure independently. Events within each closure are deterministically ordered per closure_event_ordering.

Overview: Within a closure, the Events list and Seeds list MUST be deterministically ordered so that closure display, hash derivation downstream, and tests are stable across runs regardless of Go map-iteration order.
Defined terms: eventLess — the total order over DriftEvent values used to sort Events
Requirements: R1. DeriveClosures MUST sort each closure's Events via eventLess before returning. R2. eventLess MUST define a total order with primary key Kind (numeric: groups node events before edge events naturally), then NodeID for node events, then Edge.From/Edge.To for edge events. OldHash and NewHash are tie-breakers. R3. DeriveClosures MUST sort each closure's Seeds lexicographically (sort.Strings). R4. The closures slice itself MUST be sorted by closure hash (already the case in pre-existing code). R5. Reset semantics are unaffected: EvaluateState's reset loop applies events independently; the order in which events are applied does not change the resulting baseline state.
Motivation: when two seeds produce closures that merge (same hash), the Events list is the union of both seeds' events. Without deterministic sorting, the order depended on Go map iteration, causing intermittent test failures under -race and unstable `drift todo` / `drift diff` output across runs.
See also: core.provenance_closure.

DeriveOrphans computes the set of specs that have no path from any marker — the static complement of the closure model. A spec is reachable iff some marker links to it directly (a marker→spec edge in baselineEdges), or a chain of spec→spec ref edges (from scanEdges) connects it to a marker-linked spec. Unreachable specs are orphans: their change-closure would contain no marker, meaning drift could never enforce them. baselineEdges supplies marker→spec link edges (user-curated, current via link/unlink); scanEdges supplies current spec→spec ref edges walked forward from the marker-linked seeds. Spec→spec edges inside baselineEdges are ignored — reachability reflects the LIVE spec graph, not a stale baseline snapshot. Deleted specs (baseline-only, awaiting NODE_REMOVED reset) are excluded from the orphan universe. Cycles and self-refs are harmless (visited-set prevents re-visiting). O(specs + edges). Orphans do not participate in closure derivation or drift reset; they are reported by drift todo as a separate block and flip exit code to 1. See model.provenance for the closure-reachability equivalence proof.

The core package exposes the type vocabulary the algorithm and its callers operate on. Spec{Filepath, LineNumber, ID, Module, Hash, Deleted} and Marker{Filepath, LineNumber, EndLineNumber, ID, Hash, Deleted} are the two node kinds. Edge{From, To} is the unified directed relationship: From is the citer, To is the cited. Action is a sealed interface with two concrete types — TodoAction{Scan} (read-only review) and ResetClosureAction{Hash, Scan} (sync a closure's seed events into baseline). Scan{SpecHashes, MarkerHashes, Edges} is the live-scan payload produced by the scanner. EventKind is an enum of six drift event categories (NODE_CHANGED, NODE_ADDED, NODE_REMOVED, EDGE_ADDED, EDGE_REMOVED, EDGE_BROKEN). DriftEvent carries Kind plus the NodeID (node events), Edge pointer (edge events), Old/NewHash (NODE_CHANGED), and Seed (the citer-side party that originated the event). NodeRef{ID, IsSpec, Filepath, LineNumber} is the lightweight node reference used in closure display. Closure{Hash, Nodes, Edges, Events, Seeds} is one per-seed drift set; EvaluatedState{Specs, Markers, Edges, Closures, Orphans} is the algorithm's full return shape. Sentinel errors (ErrDuplicateSpecID, ErrEdgeCycle, ErrClosureNotFound, ErrBrokenEdgeNotResettable, etc.) are the documented failure modes. See core.validate, core.provenance_closure, model.provenance.

EvaluateState is the algorithm's single entry point. It runs ctx.Validate() first (rejecting duplicate IDs, unknown edge endpoints, self-edges, duplicate edges, and directed cycles among spec-spec edges — see core.validate), then dispatches on the concrete type of ctx.Action: TodoAction routes to evaluateTodoAction (derives closures and orphans without side effects), ResetClosureAction routes to evaluateResetClosureAction (locates the closure by hash and applies its events to baseline). Any other Action type returns ErrUnknownAction wrapping the offending type. The dispatch is a Go type switch; only the two registered action types are accepted. EvaluateState never reads or writes files — it is a pure function over its context, called by the orchestrator which owns I/O. See core.todo_action, core.reset_action, core.validate.

The closure hash is the first 8 hex characters of SHA1(sortedNodeIDs ++ sortedEdgeKeys), where each element is written into the hash followed by a NUL byte (0x00) separator. canonicalEdgeKey(a, b) returns the undirected canonicalization min(a,b) + NUL + max(a,b), so two edges that differ only in direction collapse to the same key (validation rejects directed cycles among spec-spec edges, so a baseline edge and its reverse can never coexist). closureHash(sortedNodeIDs, sortedEdgeKeys) accepts both slices pre-sorted by the caller and returns the truncated hex digest; an input shorter than 8 hex chars is returned as-is (defensive, should not occur in practice). makeNodeRef(id, specsByID, markersByID) constructs a NodeRef by looking the id up first in the spec map (IsSpec=true) then the marker map (IsSpec=false), with a fallback NodeRef carrying just the ID when the node exists in neither map (defensive against closure-membership race with deletion). The hash is stable across drift-state changes as long as closure membership is unchanged; it shifts only when nodes or edges are added or removed. See core.provenance_closure.

copySpecsToMutableMap and copyMarkersToMutableMap turn the input slices into map[string]*Spec / map[string]*Marker respectively, where each map value points at a fresh copy of the struct (not an alias into the slice). This indirection is what lets DeriveClosures and evaluateResetClosureAction mutate node hashes in-place via map lookup without disturbing the caller's slice. specsFromMutableMap and markersFromMutableMap are the inverse: they gather the (mutated) map values back into a fresh slice for return. Order is not preserved across the round-trip — callers that need deterministic output sort the resulting slice themselves (e.g. DeriveClosures sorts closures by hash; evaluateResetClosureAction returns the slice to the orchestrator which saves via the state store without ordering guarantees). See core.evaluate_state, core.provenance_closure.

addEdgeIfMissing appends an edge to the slice only if no equal edge (matching both From and To) is already present; otherwise it returns the input slice unchanged. removeEdge drops every edge matching the target in EITHER direction (undirected match). The undirected match in removeEdge is safe because core.validate rejects directed cycles among spec-spec edges, so a baseline edge and its reverse can never coexist; if that invariant is ever relaxed, removeEdge must restrict itself to forward-only matching (the comment in the source restates this contract). containsString is a small linear-scan helper used during same-hash closure merging to dedupe seed IDs. These helpers are the only edge mutation primitives the algorithm uses; reset's event loop composes them. See core.reset_action.
